Put on your skates, and join the popular weekly skate tour (since 1997), a different route every week. Starts every Friday at 20:30 from the Vondelpark (near the former Filmmuseum).

For all art-house cinema lovers. All films are shown in their original language with Dutch subtitles. They have late-night and classic showings too. Just a short walk from the Albert Cuyp Market/Heineken Brouwerij, in the nice non-touristy

Largest street market in Amsterdam, and the best-known street market in the country. It is iconic for the "De Pijp" neighborhood and its working-class inhabitants. There is something for everyone here, whether you're looking for delicious D
Probably the wealthiest street in the country where Dutch celebrities go for a new pair of designer shoes. Better bring a filled wallet if you're planning to buy something here.
It's cheap and very good. If you arrive around dinnertime you probably have to wait for a table. The surroundings are depressing but the food is so good you will come back anyway.
Tasty, great value Surinamese take-out. Sandwiches. Located a short walk from the Zuidas area hotels. A few tables are also available to eat in.
Dining in the dark. All waiters are blind, and serve you dinner in a completely dark restaurant. A very weird, but actually quite fun experience.
Basic bar and beer garden
Quite tea house with a small garden.

A bit loud and boisterous for travellers looking to relax, but good for those looking to meet people from all over the world and get the true "Amsterdam Experience". Lockers require lockpads, which are not available for rent, only buy for €
Friendly youth hostel.
From single rooms to five people sharing, steep stairs and no lift, shared or private bathrooms (quite small), very close to the museums.
Surrounded by fantastic architecture with reasonable rates, even at peak. Rooms from single to quadruple and optional en suite. Comes with free coffee, breakfast and wireless internet access.
3-star hotel. All the floors are reachable by elevator. All rooms have their own private bathrooms.
Attractive, in a peaceful location in a quiet residential area.
The hotel has 70 rooms with stylish interiors and a beautiful view.
Second property by citizenM hotels, opened in 2009. Rooms include free WiFi and movies, a rainshower, and an XL kingsize bed with luxury linens.
Ticks all the main boxes for facilities but about due for a refurbishment.
Free Wi-Fi in public areas.
Five-star hotel just off the Apollolaan.
Internationally famous as the site of John Lennon's and Yoko Ono's bed-in. Nationally famous for being where Dutch artist Herman Brood killed himself.

Five-star Japanese-owned and -operated hotel with an excellent range of Japanese food, clothing, and book shops in the basement, and wireless internet in the lobby, bar, and conference rooms. The only drawback is that it's relatively distan
Bang in the middle of Amsterdam between Leidseplein, Rijksmuseum and P.C. Hooftstraat. Four-star hotel spread over several historical buildings. Parking. Very friendly staff.
Five-star hotel offers 129 guest suites spread throughout 8 floors.
A museum about the Amsterdam School architectural style, housed in a building that is probably the city's best example of that style entrance.
Not too far west of the Vondelpark, but much quieter and larger in size.
A park at the western edge of the centre, with cultural activities in a former gas factory (Westergasfabriek). Access from Haarlemmerweg.
In the Ookmeer sports fields along Ma Braunpad.
Near Seineweg.
at Nieuwpoortkade.
A restored and functioning sawmill, opposite Buyskade, west of the Jordaan.
In Zuid, the only one open for visitors
Third largest in Amsterdam with food, households, flowers and clothing.

They specialise in traditional Southern Indian cuisine, especially the eponymous 'Dosa' (a rice and lentil pancake with a variety of fillings). The food is outstanding and well worth hunting out. The dosas are exceptional and a treat worthy
International food court with 20 food-stands housed in a large building that was once a tram depot.
Traditional Dutch cuisine. The restaurant may be cramped, but it does serve some quality and rustic Dutch fare. This place is cash only.
Small ramen restaurant with friendly staff, quick service, and good selection of ramen & appetizers. Also serve beer & sake. Closes early and small seating so might want to reserve on weekends.

TonTon Club is an excellent place for a good night out. The place has a unique atmosphere with Japan as its inspiration. Upstairs there are arcades and button bashers, downstairs there's room for drinks and board games. You can also order J

Small bar with friendly staff and a cosy and candle-lit atmosphere. Selection of beers on tap and in bottles, including a triple blonde specially made for the bar. Small selection of bar food as well.
A large alternative place with lots of art on its walls. There's ping pong, a very local and fairly young crowd.
Cheap but clean hotel, close to the Van Gogh and Rijksmuseum.

Fairly large youth hostel, very clean and professional, operated by the Dutch affiliate of Hostelling International. Next to the pleasant Vondelpark, puts you on the south-western side of the city center and just a few blocks from the Van G
Trendy boutique hotel.

Near Leidseplein with tram connections and bus to airport. Near Vondelpark and Museumplein. Buffet breakfast available at extra cost. Unlimited free coffee (including koffie verkeerd, the Dutch equivalent of café au lait) for guests in the
At the border of Oud-West and the Canal District, this old-fashioned Marriott can offer a relatively attractive rate and still has a convenient location for exploring the city centre.
The hotel has 19 meeting rooms as well as 6 business suites. The hotel provides free shuttle service from and to the airport as well as free wi-fi in public areas.
Windmill on the bank of the Noordhollands Kanaal in the north, ferry from Central Station.
Museum depicting street art in a large indoor exhibition.

EYE is an institute dedicated to the preservation of film for future generations. It is the successor of the Filmmuseum. It has four film theatres with alternative screenings such as art films. In April the Imagine Film Festival is held her
A restaurant and cafe in a hall which used to be a bank.
A fish and seafood restaurant in an old factory on the banks of the river.
A redesigned aircraft hangar, turned restaurant.
An Indian and Nepalese restaurant. Vegetarian friendly.
A bar and restaurant in an old industrial area, by the river.
3-star hotel with 86 rooms.
In the hall of Amstel railway station, there are several murals created in 1939 by Dutch artist Peter Alma, including a large mural at each end of the hall with a train motif.
There are two clusters of floating houses over a body of water. These small, modern houses are linked by a grid of walkways lined with railings holding life preservers and bicycles.
Ethnographic and cultural museum about Africa, Asia and South America. Includes an excellent cafe which sells food from around the world. Tickets are discounted if reserved online.
Close to Plantage, this park holds several multicultural festivals throughout the year.
This is a large park, a little like a dune park.

The Flevopark is in the Indische Buurt, at the eastern end of the Insulindeweg, next to the Jewish cemetery, the Flevoparkbad swimming pool, and the Nieuwe Diep inlet. There are two cafés open in spring/summer/autumn time and one festival e
Frankendael is a house built in 1733 in Watergraafsmeer. The house is surrounded by a pleasant park. Take tram 9, get off at the stop "Hugo de Vrieslaan".
World-class jazz and improvised music venue, five minutes by foot from Centraal Station.
Modern music concerts and classical music with a twist. A free concert is given every second Tuesday of the month at 12:30.
In the east, behind the zoo, and was voted best market in the Netherlands.
Boutique.
For kids's clothing.

A large interior design centre that is an architectural highlight by itself. Plenty of interesting interior shops like Kartell and Kasstoor, and also don't miss the café as it has a roof terrace with a great view on the water. Free parking.
For kids' clothing.
Boutique.

Boutique.
For kids's clothing.
A deli shop annex lunch room with products from the region.
Ice cream shop.

Oktoberfest-style biergarten, so expect long tables and a wide variety of bottled beers available. It has a nice atmosphere during warm summer evenings. Try the Hamburger Deluxe or chicken menus. And come early, as it is often crowded. Rese
Italian restaurant.

Eastern and Western fusion meals with both à la carte and (on highly occupied days o­nly) a live cooking theme buffet. The restaurant has a view of the river IJ. Open 7 days per week for lunch and dinner.
Coffee bar.
A harbour-side cafe and restaurant with a view of the marina. You can just stop by for a cup of coffee, have breakfast, lunch or dinner. Stylish interior.
With over 500 bottled beers and 20 craft beers on draft, the biggest craft beer bar in Amsterdam
This nightclub is relatively close to the city centre. It has its fair share of nice nights and the view on the water is excellent.

A restaurant-bar-club, this urban and edgy den in a former newspaper office is a great place to go out at night. With nice views of the city and a varied music repertoire (alternative, jazz, funk), it's one of the hidden secrets too often o

This campground is near the city. It has camping cabins, wagonettes, tent sites and RV sites. A good store, free wifi and restaurant/bar round out the amenities. A good, clean and cheap place to stay if you do not mind walking to the bathro

This 480-bed hostel is located to the east of the city centre in a typical Amsterdam neighbourhood. Amsterdam's historic centre is less than 15 minutes away by bike or tram. The hostel is in the same building as Studio K, a budget diner and

This former university building can host up to 564 guests in twin and quadruple rooms. It has spacious social areas with creative design touches all over the building. The old lecture rooms and hall have been turned into bars and a relaxati

3 star-hotel with 192 rooms. Due to its central location, the Amsterdam RAI, Amsterdam ArenA and Ziggo Dome are very well accessible from Bastion Hotel Amsterdam Amstel. Public transport is located within a 10-minute walk.
The hotel is in the Eastern Docklands, the renewed area of the city centre.

In 1992 a Boeing 747F jumbo freighter crashed into two flats in the Bijlmer. This is a monument to the people on the ground who died or lost their houses in the disaster. 39 residents are known to have died, but due to many unregistered ill

The Johan Cruijff ArenA, built from 1993 to 1996, has a capacity of 55,865 seats during sports matches. It's the home ground of AFC Ajax, who play in the Eredivisie, the top tier of football in the Netherlands; the Dutch national team also

items.d: OSCAM is the museological platform for art, fashion, design, craftsmanship and development in Amsterdam. It has a rich background in curating art, fashion and design exhibitions with a speciality in young (sub)cultures. By involving known a

Protected monument to the original 1960s urban vision of the modernist Bijlmermeer expansion of Amsterdam. It consists of the high-rise flats Gooioord, Groeneveen, Grubbehoeve, Kikkenstein, Kleiburg and Kruitberg, the brutalist metro viaduc

Large-scale music venue with plenty of international stars having performed here. More "headliners" are booked in Amsterdam for AFAS Live than any other venue. Best reached by train or metro (station Amsterdam Bijlmer ArenA).
Indoor music venue.
One of the largest cinemas in the country, and it also has IMAX movies.

Recreational area and nature reserve with a lake and water-sports centre. The centre offers facilities for canoeing, swimming, rowing, sailing and a surfing school. Explore the park (5 km around the lake) by foot, bicycle or horseback. On t

A well-equipped outdoor gym with permanent workout stations, made out of green plastic & metal. If you spend some time in Bijlmer, this is a good spot to workout for free during the daytime, and talk to locals. Just beside the running track

Largest shopping centre in Zuidoost and indeed one of the largest in Amsterdam. All the usual big chain shops, but toward the eastern end, particularly in the "Shopper Hal" a lot of local/Caribbean/African places. Be sure to try the sausage

On the west side of the railway so caters less to locals than people from elsewhere in town or indeed the country, consisting of a number of very large stores. Could be useful if in need of electronics or sporting equipment.

One of the larger local shopping centers. The main attraction is the metro line, which passes over the shopping street and disappears through a building on the eastern side. You'll also be sure to spot the herons (reigers) the area is named
Surinamese and Indonesian cuisine. Very good Moksi Meti (marinated pork and sausages with noodles). Popular with the locals. Take-away.
Sandwich bar. Mainly caters to office workers in surrounding buildings. Try the hummus & sun-dried tomato.
One of the few Ghanaian snack bars in Amsterdam. Specializes in Kenkey (a sort of sourdough dumpling), but has a wide range of West-African cuisine at very reasonable prices.

Relatively up-market Turkish/Mediterranean restaurant in the fancy new building opposite station Bijlmer-Arena. Great food, presentation and service - definitely worth the price. On cold days, avoid sitting anywhere near the door as it freq

Inevitably, hipsters have even found their way into the Bijlmer. Part-funded by crowdfunding. Very worthy 'Swedish style' coffee house. Coffee, biological lemonade and cakes. Also showcases art by local artists.

Restaurant dedicated to circular economy. Occupies a formerly derelict building, all furnishings are second-hand, and as much food as possible is home-grown or locally sourced. Profits are invested in local community initiatives, and the wh
Surinamese Caribbean vegan food made by a local collective. Also delivers within Zuidoost and Diemen.

In 2015 the first monastery - the Kleiklooster - opened in the Bijlmer, and as good monks do, they started brewing beer. Good beer, if somewhat eccentric. This is their tasting hall where you can sample the current Kleiburg brews. Avoid lat
Large cafe under the Hampton/Hilton hotel. During the day mainly caters to the nearby office crowd, but in the evenings it gets more local.
First - and as of September 2021, only - coffee shop in Zuidoost. Caters to locals, day trippers to large venues nearby and tourists in the surrounding hotels. Take-away or smoke in.
The capital's largest campsite.

Immediately adjacent to metro station Bullewijk, 5 min walk from train station Amsterdam Bijlmer-Arena. Free wifi. Free parking. No curfew. This hostel is the largest in Amsterdam, opened in 2015 in a completely renovated former office buil
3-star hotel. Free Wi-Fi. Free parking.
3-star hotel. Free parking. 8 conference rooms. Restaurant. The bar is open till 01:00.
Exactly what you'd expect from Easy - affordable, no-frills but generally clean.

items.d: Surprisingly affordable, straight across from Bijlmer Arena station.
